summary: D-100 is what D-096 clause 3 (B) reserved and nothing more. Every attack line in the dispatch fails against the bytes. The entry does not grant, and says so operatively rather than only in recital: clause 1 makes the grant a later user-made act, and adds the anti-ratchet that overturning D-100 neither creates a grant nor overturns D-096. The D-054 / D-057 exclusion is not decorative — I read D-054 and its subject line confines it to 'condition 1 owner-recording for preview Route B only', so the exclusion states a real boundary rather than reciting one. The five eligible candidates are exactly D-096's five, and the per-candidate role column is not the coordinator's invention: each entry reproduces the candidate artifact's own ownerWhoMustRecord field verbatim, including the composite DR-106/109/113 map. I checked this specifically because a mechanics entry is the natural place to widen roles quietly, and it does not. All fifteen digests I could verify against live bytes verify: five candidates, ten independent verdict files, plus COORD, file 08, freeze, and three commits. The two advisories below are drafting-precision gaps in what a later entry must pin; neither opens an authorization path, and both are independently fenced by D-096 clauses that D-100 leaves unoverturned.

attackLinesAndOutcomes.attack: treats this as a grant, or as D-054 / D-057 covering these rows
attackLinesAndOutcomes.reasoning: Clause 1 states the file does not grant and locates D-096 (A) in a later user-made express act. Clause 2 lists 'D-054 / D-057 are not cited as that grant' as a hard precondition, and the Alternatives section rejects the move citing ADV-D095-T2-01. I confirmed the exclusion is substantive by reading D-054, whose Subject line reads 'condition 1 owner-recording for preview Route B only' — condition 2 is outside it on the amendment's own terms.

'A mechanics entry alone never grants' appears in clause 1 and matches D-096 clause 3 verbatim in substance. Clause 6 sets readiness effect to zero and records no row. The anti-ratchet sentence — overturning D-100 creates no grant — closes the inverse route, which is the one a mechanics entry would most plausibly leak through.

The table confines DR-116 to 'Product security (Route C only)' — which is the artifact's own ownerWhoMustRecord string, not a widening — and clause 3 restates 'DR-116 Route C does not generalize.' D-096 clause 3's fence against generalizing to the other security / release / evidence / platform roles is reproduced, not relaxed.

advisoriesList.location: Clause 4, first bullet — 'file-08 owner role(s) being recorded'
advisoriesList.observation: Clause 4 requires every later owner-recording entry to pin the 'file-08 owner role(s) being recorded'. Four of the five candidates have a file-08 row, but the Windows candidate does not. Its artifact records registerRow as 'D-002 platform set — Windows' and states 'Does not add or remove a file-08 row', and D-096 clause 4 says outright that 'Windows is not a file-08 row and is not SATISFIED as one'. For that candidate the pin as literally worded has no referent. I checked this across all five rather than assuming the composite row was the odd one out, and Windows is the only mismatch.
advisoriesList.whyNotBlocking: It cannot open an authorization path. Clause 5 forbids editing file 08, and D-096 clause 4 remains unoverturned by D-100's own recital, so a later drafter who reached for a file-08 row to satisfy the pin would be refused by D-096 before D-100 mattered. The defect is that the pin invites the reach at all.
advisoriesList.suggestedRepairIfEverRevisited: Word the pin as 'file-08 owner role(s), or for the Windows platform set the named owner roles, being recorded' — or add a parenthetical that Windows carries owner roles without a file-08 row.

advisoriesList.location: Clause 2 ('still at its recorded digest') read against clause 5 ('Record the candidate as the owner-recorded … explicit deferral')
advisoriesList.observation: Clause 2 conditions eligibility on the candidate still hashing to its recorded digest, and clause 4 requires the later entry to pin that digest. But those frozen bytes internally declare status 'CANDIDATE-NOT-RECORDED', binds 'NOTHING', and sealRecommendation 'DO-NOT-SEAL' — the three properties D-096 clause 2 fixed. D-100 is silent on how the register's owner-recorded state and the artifact's own self-description coexist afterwards, and therefore on whether the artifact bytes may ever be updated to reflect the recording.
advisoriesList.whyNotBlocking: The silence is self-limiting rather than permissive. Editing the artifact would break the digest precondition in clause 2 and the pin in clause 4, so the ambiguity resolves against mutation on D-100's own terms. D-096 clause 2's DO-NOT-SEAL also survives untouched. No authority is gained either way; the gap is housekeeping for a later entry, not a leak.
advisoriesList.suggestedRepairIfEverRevisited: One sentence in clause 5 stating that the register entry is authoritative for recording status and that the candidate artifact's bytes stay frozen at the recorded digest.

notes.observation: D-097 clause 2 says 'Do not record the elided D-054 quotations as a new amendment' — the precise vector its two MUST-FIXes closed. D-100 clause 2 excludes D-054 / D-057 by name but does not restate that prohibition, so on D-100's face a new amendment recycling the same 2026-08-14 words is not the excluded instrument.
notes.whyNotAFinding: Doubly fenced already. Those words name no owner role at all, so such an amendment could not clear clause 2's requirement that the grant 'expressly covers every named role for the candidate being recorded'; and D-100's recital leaves D-097 unoverturned, so D-097 clause 2 continues to bind on its own. Recording it here would be belt-and-braces, not repair.

notes.observation: D-100 states no condition-4 figure. D-096 and D-097 both recite 'Condition 4 stays 16 of 18 PARTLY MET', which D-102 superseded to 18 of 18 standing MET. By omitting condition 4 entirely rather than copying the recital forward, D-100 avoids carrying a stale readiness figure into a new entry. Worth recording as correct behaviour observed, not a defect.

structuralObservation: D-100 is deliberately the condition-2 analogue of D-057, and the parallel holds where it should: preconditions, pins, own D-000 cycle and commit, a prior separately committed coordinator recording, and revocation requiring the owner's supersession plus reconciliation of every dependent MF-6 note. The one asymmetry is the important one and is handled correctly. D-057 could be adopted because its authority, user-made D-054, was already live; D-100's authority does not exist yet. Rather than paper over that, D-100 makes the missing grant a standing precondition and states that its own overturn cannot manufacture one. That is the shape D-096 clause 3 asked for when it split (A) from (B) and allowed (B) to be adopted alone.
consentStatement: CONSENT. No MUST-FIX. No SHOULD-FIX. Two advisories and two notes, none of which conditions consent. D-100 grants nothing, records no row, satisfies no D-096 (A), and leaves condition 2 unchanged.
